title: OpenAI offers $5 million for independent research on AI and teen development
friendlyTitle: OpenAI will fund studies about how AI affects teenagers
summary: OpenAI is accepting worldwide proposals on how generative AI affects people aged 13–17, with individual grants up to $1 million and applications due October 6. Eligible work includes well-being, relationships, patterns of use and safeguards, with ethics review, consent, privacy and safeguarding requirements for research involving minors.
friendlySummary: Researchers can apply for part of a $5 million grant program to study AI use by 13- to 17-year-olds. Projects must explain how they will protect young people, private information and informed consent.
whyItMatters: Families, schools and product teams need evidence that distinguishes different ages, uses and circumstances rather than treating all teen AI use as one category. Researchers should note that OpenAI funds and administers the program, disclosures are required, and public publication is encouraged but not mandatory.
friendlyWhyItMatters: Parents, schools and app makers need better evidence about when AI helps or harms teenagers. The studies should be judged carefully because the company making ChatGPT is paying for them.
